recommendation: Keep the no-change audit as-is. No core follow-up is needed unless a future work-group decision reopens the broader participant-pattern question of whether Endpoint should remain a recipient target.
issue_request: FHIR-22630 was a Published/Persuasive with Modification Patient Care change request asking that CommunicationRequest allow Endpoint as a recipient; the final resolution broadened the request so both Communication and CommunicationRequest allow Endpoint as recipient and sender/informationProvider.
initial_application: The issue was initially applied by bacd75ef4fb5fe08e2b16d04e3fd5bfd278fc916, which added Endpoint to the old spreadsheet target-type lists and GF#22630 committee notes for Communication.recipient, Communication.sender, CommunicationRequest.recipient, and CommunicationRequest.informationProvider. Later source refactoring preserved the change in the current StructureDefinition XML files.
additional_context: Communication and CommunicationRequest are active, approved resources in source/fhir.ini. Current StructureDefinitions include Endpoint targetProfile entries and GF#22630 notes on all affected elements, and current active notes pages list Endpoint in the relevant sender/informationProvider and recipient summaries. Confluence minutes confirm the Patient Care resolution; later participant-pattern discussion raised concerns but no discovered final reversal, and later PA/CDEX minutes cite Endpoint as a CommunicationRequest.recipient use case.
reconciliation: No source change was made because the authoritative element definitions and active notes already convey the final FHIR-22630 rule.

related_jiras.note: Related sender/receiver rename and wording work explains why current CommunicationRequest source uses informationProvider rather than sender.
